# Queue rebuilds as durable jobs

## Intent

A rebuild of a carry-patch workspace can take minutes and can fail for reasons that pass: an upstream that is unreachable, a lost race on a ref, a restart of the hub. A caller must be able to ask for a rebuild once and trust that it will run: the request is recorded before it is answered, it survives a restart, it is retried with growing delays, and there is never more than one pending rebuild per workspace. This package gives the hub a durable job queue with exactly those guarantees, and puts the rebuild job in front of callers: submit, list, read, cancel and requeue, over the REST API and the `parley rebuild` commands.

## Goals

- A job is stored in the transactional store before the request that created it is answered, and is readable after the store is closed and opened again.
- A job moves only along the state machine `queued`, `running`, `failed`, `completed`, `dead_letter`, `cancelled`; `failed` is never an end state.
- A retryable failure is retried after `min(2 s × 2ⁿ, 2 h)` at most 20 times; the 21st retryable failure, and any permanent failure, dead-letters the job.
- At most one rebuild job per workspace is `queued`, `running` or `failed`, with the single exception of the follow-up a running rebuild queues for itself.
- At most 4 jobs run at once across the hub and at most one per workspace; a queued job starts within 5 seconds when a worker is free.
- A job found `running` when the hub starts returns to `queued` with its `retry_count` unchanged and runs again from the start.
- `POST /workspaces/:slug/rebuild` answers `202` with the rebuild job record; `GET …/rebuilds`, `GET …/rebuilds/:id`, `DELETE …/rebuilds/:id` and `POST …/rebuilds/:id/requeue` list, read, cancel and requeue jobs.
- `parley rebuild submit|list|status|cancel|requeue` call those routes; `--wait` waits through `failed` and ends only on `completed`, `dead_letter` or `cancelled`.
- Every other package that queues a rebuild uses one enqueue operation with the same dedup.

## Non-goals

- What a rebuild does (upstream fetch, patch order, conflicts, publication, the stale-input check, the push of the integration branch), the events `parley.rebuild.complete`, `parley.rebuild.fail`, `parley.rebuild.push_failed` and `parley.rebuild.followup`, and which failures are permanent or retryable (CP-FR-040 to CP-FR-055): package 34 `rebuild_execution`. This package runs jobs through a handler interface and gives the handler the hooks those events need.

- The callers of the shared enqueue other than `POST …/rebuild`: sync (package 36 `carry_patch_sync`), reset to origin (package 32 `patch_maintenance`), updates of a patch branch and landing on one (package 37 `carry_patch_push_control`), the stale-input follow-up (package 34). Each decides what it answers when the enqueue reports a duplicate.
- Carry-patch workspace creation, the patch list and the common carry-patch precondition check (CP-FR-001 to CP-FR-018): package 31 `carry_patch_setup_and_patches`. This package calls that check.
- Discarding what an interrupted rebuild left in the repository at start (the second half of CP-FR-095), the purge of deleted patches and the patch-status summary (CP-FR-089 to CP-FR-097): package 38 `carry_patch_rerere_and_maintenance`.
- The workspace settings `rebuild_strategy` and `rebuild_fail_mode` (their storage and validation): package 11 `workspace_read_update_settings`. This package reads them.
- The removal step of a workspace delete: package 14 `workspace_archive_reclone_delete`. This package supplies the remover for job records.

## Background

The repository holds no code yet; every file named here is new, except the files earlier packages create and this package extends (`internal/hub/` of package 03 for the start hook and background work, the router of `internal/server/`, the root command of `internal/cli/`).

The source PRD (`docs/prd/10_carry_patch.md`) describes the durable job model in §10.3.4, the rebuild job record in §10.3.5, rebuild submit in CP-FR-034 to CP-FR-039, list, get, cancel and requeue in CP-FR-056 to CP-FR-059, the routes in §10.5, the commands in §10.6, the workers and the metric in §10.7 and the events in §10.8. Rebuild is the only job type in this version; the model is written so that it can carry other types later.

The work falls into two places:

- `internal/jobs/` holds the general queue: the job record (`job.go`), its persistence and the schema migration registered with `internal/store/` (`store.go`), enqueue and dedup (`enqueue.go`), the dispatcher and the workers (`queue.go`), the settlement of an attempt and the retry policy (`settle.go`), crash recovery and shutdown (`lifecycle.go`). It knows nothing about rebuilds: a job has a type, a workspace, a payload document and a result document, and is executed by the handler registered for its type.
- `internal/carrypatch/` holds what is specific to rebuild jobs: the shared enqueue (`rebuild_enqueue.go`), the rebuild job record (`rebuild_record.go`) and the five routes (`rebuild_routes.go`). The handler that performs a rebuild is package 34's and is registered under the job type `rebuild`.

The commands live in `internal/cli/rebuild.go`. Tests live beside the code (`internal/jobs/queue_test.go`, `internal/carrypatch/rebuild_routes_test.go`, `internal/cli/rebuild_test.go`); the end-to-end tests are in `test/e2e/rebuild_jobs_test.go`.

## Requirements

### The job and its states (§10.3.4)

A job has an id (UUID), a type, a workspace slug, a status, a payload document fixed at enqueue, a result document the handler writes, `retry_count`, `next_attempt_at`, the text of the last failure (`error`), an optional detail document of the last failure, `created_at`, `updated_at` and `completed_at`.

| Status | Meaning | Final |
|---|---|---|
| `queued` | Waiting for a worker. | no |
| `running` | A worker is executing it. | no |
| `failed` | The last attempt failed with a retryable error. The job is waiting to retry. | no |
| `completed` | Succeeded. The result is stored. | yes |
| `dead_letter` | Failed for good: a permanent error, or retries exhausted. Can be requeued. | yes, until requeued |
| `cancelled` | Cancelled while queued. | yes |

| From | To | Trigger |
|---|---|---|
| (new) | `queued` | Enqueue. |
| `queued` | `running` | A worker claims the job. One worker at most claims a given job. |
| `queued` | `cancelled` | Cancel. |
| `running` | `completed` | The attempt succeeded. |
| `running` | `failed` | Retryable error with retries left. `retry_count` goes up by one and `next_attempt_at` is set. |
| `running` | `dead_letter` | Permanent error, or a retryable error with no retries left. |
| `failed` | `queued` | `next_attempt_at` is reached. |
| `running` | `queued` | The hub starts and finds the job still marked running. `retry_count` is unchanged. |
| `dead_letter` | `queued` | Requeue. `retry_count` returns to 0. |

No other transition exists. `failed` is never final: nothing in the hub or the CLI treats it as an end state.

`completed_at` is set when the job reaches `completed`, `dead_letter` or `cancelled`, and is null otherwise, also after a requeue. `next_attempt_at` is set only while the job is `failed`. `error` is cleared when the job completes or is requeued; it is kept while the job is retried.

### Enqueue and dedup (§10.3.4, CP-FR-039)

Enqueue stores a new job as `queued` with `retry_count` 0, inside the store transaction of its caller, so that the job and the event that reports it are committed together and before the request is answered.

At most one job per job type and workspace may be `queued`, `running` or `failed`. An enqueue that would create a second one is refused: it stores nothing and reports a duplicate that names the existing job's id. Of several concurrent enqueues for one workspace exactly one stores a job.

The single exception is the follow-up: an enqueue that names a job of the same type and workspace that is `running`, while that job is the only one of the workspace that is `queued`, `running` or `failed`. It is stored as `queued` and starts only after the running job has ended. A follow-up that names a job that is not `running`, or that comes while another follow-up is already queued, is a duplicate.

### Workers (§10.3.4, §10.7)

The hub runs the jobs itself; there is no separate worker process. A dispatcher looks for work at least once per second and whenever a job was queued. A queued job starts within 5 seconds when a worker is free.

- At most 4 jobs run at once across the hub.
- At most one job per job type and workspace runs at a time: a queued job is not claimed while another job of its type and workspace is `running`.
- Queued jobs are claimed oldest first.
- A given job is claimed by at most one worker. A claim sets the status to `running` and empties the result document.
- A queued job whose type has no registered handler is not claimed and stays `queued`.
- A `failed` job whose `next_attempt_at` is reached returns to `queued` with `next_attempt_at` null, and is then claimed like any queued job.

### The outcome of an attempt (§10.3.4)

The handler receives the job and a context, may store a result document on the running job at any time (readers see it at once), and returns nil or an error. An error is retryable unless the handler marked it permanent; an error may carry a detail document.

- **Success.** The job becomes `completed`; `error` and the failure detail are cleared; `completed_at` is set.
- **Retryable failure with `retry_count` below 20.** The job becomes `failed`; `retry_count` goes up by one; `next_attempt_at` is the present plus the delay; `error` holds the failure's text. The delay after the n-th retryable failure is `min(2 s × 2ⁿ, 2 h)`: 4 s, 8 s, 16 s, … 4096 s after the 11th, and 2 h from the 12th on.
- **Retryable failure with `retry_count` 20** (the 21st). The job becomes `dead_letter` with `retry_count` still 20.
- **Permanent failure.** The job becomes `dead_letter` at once; `retry_count` is unchanged; it is not retried.
- **A handler that panics** counts as a retryable failure whose `error` names the panic; the hub keeps running.

On every failure the detail document is replaced by the one the error carries, or cleared when it carries none. `dead_letter` sets `completed_at`.

Each settlement is one store transaction. Inside it the queue calls the settlement hook the handler's type registered, with the job as it now is and whether it will be retried, so that the type's events are written with the state change. A hook that fails has its own writes undone and is logged; the settlement still commits.

### Crash recovery and shutdown (§10.3.4, CP-FR-095, CP-FR-096)

At start, before any worker claims a job, every job found `running` returns to `queued` with `retry_count`, `error` and the payload unchanged. It then runs again from the start. This is safe for rebuilds because a rebuild changes nothing visible until it publishes.

At shutdown the queue claims no further job and gives running handlers 30 seconds. The outcome of a handler that returns within that time is settled as usual. After 30 seconds the contexts of the remaining handlers are cancelled and the queue stops without settling them: their jobs stay `running` in the store and are recovered at the next start.

### Counts and removal (§10.3.4, §10.7)

The queue reports the number of jobs for each job type and each of the six statuses, zero included; this is the source of the metric `parley_jobqueue_depth{type,status}`.

Job records are kept for as long as the workspace exists. The queue removes all jobs of a workspace inside the transaction of the workspace's removal. A handler still running for a removed job has its context cancelled, and its outcome is dropped.

### The rebuild job record (§10.3.5)

Every rebuild route that returns a job returns this object with every field present (`null` when unset).

| Field | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `id` | UUID | Job id. |
| `workspace_slug` | string | |
| `status` | enum | One of the six statuses. |
| `strategy` | `rebase` \| `merge` | Captured at enqueue. |
| `fail_mode` | `fail_fast` \| `continue` | Captured at enqueue. |
| `integration_branch` | string | Captured at enqueue. |
| `submitted_by` | string | A user id, or `system:push`, `system:land`, `system:followup`. |
| `retry_count` | integer | Retryable failures so far. |
| `next_attempt_at` | timestamp, nullable | Set only while `failed`. |
| `error` | string, nullable | Text of the last failure. |
| `conflict` | conflict report, nullable | The detail document of the last failure. |
| `created_at`, `updated_at` | timestamp | |
| `completed_at` | timestamp, nullable | |
| `upstream_head_sha`, `integration_head_sha`, `previous_integration_head_sha` | string, nullable | From the result document. |
| `patches_applied`, `patches_skipped`, `patches_conflicted`, `patches_removed` | integer | From the result document; 0 when it has none. |
| `integration_branch_pushed` | boolean | From the result document; `false` when it has none. |
| `patch_results` | array | From the result document; `[]` when it has none. |

The first four captured fields are the job's payload. The fields "from the result document" are written by the rebuild handler of package 34 under these same names; this package returns what the document holds and the stated defaults for what it lacks.

### Rebuild submit (CP-FR-034 to CP-FR-039)

`POST /workspaces/:slug/rebuild` queues a rebuild. Scope `rebuilds:write`; write access. The body is optional: no body, an empty body and `{}` are equal. `strategy` must be `rebase` or `merge`; `fail_mode` must be `fail_fast` or `continue`; any other value is `400` `invalid_request`. An omitted, null or empty value falls back to the workspace setting `rebuild_strategy` (default `rebase`) or `rebuild_fail_mode` (default `fail_fast`).

After validation and the common carry-patch checks (below), in this order:

1. A workspace with no patch in `active` or `conflict` has nothing to rebuild: `400` `no_active_patches`.
2. A workspace that already has a rebuild job `queued`, `running` or `failed`: `409` `concurrent_rebuild`, and the message names the existing job's id.

Otherwise the answer is `202` with the job record: `status` `queued`, `submitted_by` the caller's user id, `retry_count` 0. Strategy, fail mode and integration branch are captured in the job; later changes of the settings do not affect a job that exists. The hub writes `parley.rebuild.enqueue` in the same transaction as the job: `resource_type` `rebuild`, `resource_id` the job id, actor the caller, metadata `submitted_by`, `strategy`, `fail_mode`, `patch_count`.

The route accepts `Idempotency-Key`: a replay answers `200` with the original job record and queues nothing.

**The shared enqueue.** Every source of a rebuild uses one operation with the same dedup. It takes the workspace, an optional strategy and fail mode (falling back to the settings), `submitted_by`, the actor and session of the event, and, for a follow-up, the running job it follows. It does not apply the `no_active_patches` check: automatic triggers queue a rebuild also when every patch is disabled or merged (CP-FR-055). On a duplicate it stores nothing, writes no event and reports the existing job's id; the source decides what to answer:

| Source | `submitted_by` | Event actor | On duplicate |
|---|---|---|---|
| `POST …/rebuild` | caller's user id | caller | `409` `concurrent_rebuild` |
| Sync, reset to origin | caller's user id | caller | skipped by the source |
| Update of a patch branch | `system:push` | `system` | skipped by the source |
| Landing on a patch branch | `system:land` | `system` | skipped by the source |
| Stale-input follow-up | `system:followup` | `system` | skipped by the source |

### Rebuild list and get (CP-FR-056, CP-FR-057)

`GET /workspaces/:slug/rebuilds` returns the rebuild jobs of the workspace as `{"items":[job,…],"next_cursor":…}`, newest `created_at` first. Scope `rebuilds:read`; read access. Query: `status` (one of the six statuses; any other value is `400` `invalid_request`), `limit`, `cursor`.

`GET /workspaces/:slug/rebuilds/:id` returns the job record. A job that is `running` shows the result document as the handler last stored it.

On every job route an id that names no job, names a job of another workspace, or is not a UUID is `404` `not_found` with the message `rebuild job not found`.

### Cancel and requeue (CP-FR-058, CP-FR-059)

`DELETE /workspaces/:slug/rebuilds/:id` cancels a queued job. Scope `rebuilds:write`. A `queued` job becomes `cancelled`, `completed_at` is set, the answer is `200` with the job record, and `parley.rebuild.cancel` is written (actor the caller, no metadata). Any other status, including a job a worker claimed a moment earlier, is `409` `job_not_cancellable`. Cancel and claim exclude each other: a cancelled job's handler is never called.

`POST /workspaces/:slug/rebuilds/:id/requeue` (no body; scope `rebuilds:write`) moves a `dead_letter` job back to `queued` with `retry_count` 0, `error`, `conflict` and `completed_at` null, and writes `parley.rebuild.requeue` (actor the caller, no metadata). The answer is `200` with the job record. The job keeps its id, `created_at`, strategy, fail mode, integration branch and `submitted_by`, and reads fresh inputs when it runs. Any status other than `dead_letter` is `409` `job_not_requeueable`. While another rebuild job of the workspace is `queued`, `running` or `failed`, requeue is `409` `concurrent_rebuild`.

### Access and common checks (CP-FR-006 to CP-FR-008, as they apply to these five routes)

The routes follow the global check order. What a caller observes:

| Case | Answer |
|---|---|
| PAT without `rebuilds:read` on a read route, or without `rebuilds:write` on a write route | `403` `insufficient_scope` |
| No access to the workspace, or unknown slug | `404` `not_found` |
| Read access only, on a write route | `403` `forbidden` |
| Workspace not in carry-patch mode (a standard workspace, a task fork) | `400` `workspace_mode_mismatch` |
| Write route, workspace `pending`, `cloning`, or with a running reclone, archive or delete | `409` `workspace_busy` |
| Write route, workspace `failed` | `409` `workspace_not_ready` |
| Write route, workspace `archived` | `409` `workspace_archived` |

The two read routes work in every workspace state. Request validation (`400` `invalid_request`) comes before the mode check; the mode check before the status check; both before the job lookup (`404`) and before `no_active_patches`, `concurrent_rebuild`, `job_not_cancellable` and `job_not_requeueable`.

### CLI (§10.6)

The global CLI conventions apply. Unless stated, a command prints the hub's response.

| Command | Flags | Calls |
|---|---|---|
| `parley rebuild submit <workspace-slug>` | `--strategy <rebase\|merge>`, `--fail-mode <fail_fast\|continue>`, `--wait`, `--timeout` (default 5m), `--poll-interval` (default 5s) | `POST /workspaces/:slug/rebuild`; a flag that was not given is not sent |
| `parley rebuild list <workspace-slug>` | `--status <status>` | `GET /workspaces/:slug/rebuilds` |
| `parley rebuild status <workspace-slug> <rebuild-id>` | | `GET /workspaces/:slug/rebuilds/:id` |
| `parley rebuild cancel <workspace-slug> <rebuild-id>` | | `DELETE /workspaces/:slug/rebuilds/:id` |
| `parley rebuild requeue <workspace-slug> <rebuild-id>` | `--wait`, `--timeout`, `--poll-interval`, as for `submit` | `POST /workspaces/:slug/rebuilds/:id/requeue` |

With `--wait`, `submit` and `requeue` then poll `GET /workspaces/:slug/rebuilds/:id` until the job is `completed`, `dead_letter` or `cancelled`. `failed` means the job waits to retry, so polling continues. The output is the final job record. Exit status 0 when the job is queued (no `--wait`) or `completed`; 1 when the wait ends in `dead_letter` or `cancelled` (the final record on stdout, `wait_failed` on stderr) or times out (nothing on stdout, `wait_timeout` on stderr).

A value of `--strategy`, `--fail-mode` or `--status` outside its list, and a wrong number of arguments, is a usage error: exit status 2, no request.

### End-to-end flows

1. **Submit and wait through a retry.** A developer runs `parley rebuild submit <slug> --wait` on a carry-patch workspace with one active patch. The CLI posts; `parleyd` stores the job and `parley.rebuild.enqueue` and answers `202`; a worker claims the job and runs the handler, which fails with a retryable error; the job is `failed` with `retry_count` 1 and `next_attempt_at` 4 seconds later; the CLI keeps polling; the job returns to `queued`, runs again and completes; the CLI prints the final record with `status` `completed` and exits 0.
2. **Restart during a run.** An agent posts a rebuild; a worker claims it; the hub stops before the handler returns; the hub starts again; the job returns to `queued` with `retry_count` 0, is claimed and its handler runs from the start; the agent reads the job and sees `completed`.
3. **Dead letter, cancel and requeue.** An agent posts a rebuild; the handler fails with a permanent error and the job is `dead_letter`; the agent posts a second rebuild and gets `202`; a requeue of the first job is `409` `concurrent_rebuild`; the agent cancels the second job (`200`, `cancelled`); a second cancel is `409` `job_not_cancellable`; the requeue of the first job now answers `200` with `status` `queued` and `retry_count` 0; the event log holds two `parley.rebuild.enqueue`, one `parley.rebuild.cancel` and one `parley.rebuild.requeue`.

## Design Decisions

1. **Project decisions relied on.** Go; the transactional store is SQLite through `internal/store`; HTTP is `net/http`; the CLI is cobra through the command helper of package 09; tests use `testing`, `net/http/httptest` and a real store in `t.TempDir()`; code takes a replaceable clock.
2. **Two layers.** `internal/jobs` is a general queue that knows a job's type, workspace, payload and result as opaque JSON documents; `internal/carrypatch` gives rebuild jobs their fields and routes. Why: §10.3.4 says the model must carry other types later.
3. **The handler interface.** A type registers a handler with two operations: one that runs an attempt (context and job in, error out) and one settlement hook called inside the transaction of each settlement with the job and whether it will be retried. An error is retryable unless wrapped as permanent; an error may carry a detail document. Why: package 34 must write `parley.rebuild.complete` and `parley.rebuild.fail` with the state change (§10.8), and only the queue knows `will_retry`.
4. **A failing settlement hook does not block the settlement.** Its writes are undone, the failure is logged, the state change commits. Why: a job stuck in `running` would block the workspace until a restart; package 14 treats its collaborators the same way.
5. **Dedup and "one at a time" are per job type and workspace.** The PRD says "per workspace" with one job type; this is the same rule for a second type.
6. **`retry_count` stays 20 when the 21st retryable failure dead-letters the job.** Why: the transition table raises it only on `running` to `failed`.
7. **A claim empties the result document.** Why: `patch_results` is "the results so far" of the running attempt, and an attempt runs from the start.
8. **`error` survives a retry and crash recovery** and is cleared only by completion and requeue, as §10.3.5 states.
9. **A panic in a handler is a retryable failure.** Why: library code must not end the process, and the cause may pass.
10. **A type without a handler leaves its jobs `queued`.** Why: the simplest behaviour, and it lets this package work before package 34 registers the rebuild handler.
11. **Dispatcher.** It passes at least once per second and is woken by an enqueue, a requeue and the end of an attempt; tests run single passes with a controlled clock. Why: "a queued job starts within a few seconds" (§10.7), fixed here at 5 seconds.
12. **Claim order** is `created_at` ascending, then id. The PRD does not state one.
13. **Shutdown.** Outcomes that arrive within the 30-second grace are settled; handlers still running at its end are cancelled and not settled, so their jobs are recovered at the next start with `retry_count` unchanged (CP-FR-096). Package 03 names this package as the one that stops rebuild jobs at shutdown; the queue is registered as background work with a 30-second grace and crash recovery as a start hook.
14. **Order of the submit checks:** `no_active_patches` before `concurrent_rebuild`, the order of CP-FR-035 and CP-FR-037.
15. **Requeue checks the job's own status before the workspace's other jobs:** a job that is not `dead_letter` answers `job_not_requeueable` also when another job is pending.
16. **The job lookup comes after the mode and status checks** (CP-FR-008 puts those directly after validation). A job id that is not a UUID is `404`, like an unknown id.
17. **List order** is `created_at` descending, then id descending, so that the order is total (PLAT-FR-014).
18. **`patch_count`** in `parley.rebuild.enqueue` is the number of patches in `active` or `conflict` when the job is queued. The PRD names the member only.
19. **An empty or null `strategy` or `fail_mode`** falls back to the setting ("omitted or empty", CP-FR-034); a value of another JSON type is `400` `invalid_request`.
20. **The CLI checks enumerated flag values itself** (exit status 2, no request), because PLAT-FR-092 lists "invalid flag value" as a usage error.
21. **The command that reads one job is `parley rebuild status`**, as §10.6 and appendix B name it.
22. **Job ids** are random UUIDs (version 4) made with `crypto/rand`; no library.
23. **Removal with the workspace.** The queue exports the remover and registers it with the removers of owned data of package 14 (`internal/workspace/teardown.go`), which run inside the workspace's delete transaction.
24. **The shared enqueue implements `RebuildEnqueuer` of package 31.** Package 31 declares the interface, its options and result types and a default that queues nothing; `EnqueueRebuild` here is the implementation, registered when the hub is composed. Packages 32, 34, 36 and 37 call the interface, so package 32 needs no dependency on this package.
25. **The session of a trigger is kept in the job's payload**, beside the four captured fields, and is not part of the job record. §10.8 says a rebuild queued by a push or a landing carries that session; package 34 reads it for the job's events.
26. **One owner for start and shutdown (CP-FR-095, CP-FR-096).** This package owns the return of `running` jobs to `queued` at start, the stop of claiming at shutdown and the 30-second grace, with their criteria. Package 38 owns only the discard of what an interrupted rebuild left in the repository, as a start hook of its own, and specifies no queue behaviour.
27. **A follow-up is queued while the job it follows is still `running`.** The settlement hook sees the job as settled, so package 34 calls the enqueue with the follow-up-of id before its run operation returns, and writes `parley.rebuild.followup` in the hook.
28. **Profile: full.**

## Dependencies

- Package 31 `carry_patch_setup_and_patches` (draft): carry-patch workspaces, the patch list (for `no_active_patches` and `patch_count`), the integration branch name (`IntegrationBranch`), the `RebuildEnqueuer` interface and the common carry-patch precondition check.
- Package 09 `cli_foundation` (draft): the command helper, the HTTP client, output, exit codes and the shared `--wait`.
- Package 52 `durable_event_log_and_stream` (draft): writing an event in the transaction of its state change.
- Package 14 `workspace_archive_reclone_delete` (draft): the removers of owned data, with which the remover of job records is registered.
- Used through those: package 02 (error envelope, lists, idempotency), package 03 (`internal/hub` start hooks and background work, `internal/store`), package 07 (access), package 11 (workspace settings).
- Package 34 `rebuild_execution` depends on this package and registers the rebuild handler.

## Glossary

- **Hub**: The `parleyd` server.
- **Workspace**: A repository the hub holds, identified by its `slug`. Either a registered repository or a task fork.
- **Carry-patch workspace**: A workspace that tracks an upstream project and keeps an ordered list of patches on top of it.
- **Integration branch**: For a carry-patch workspace, the branch the hub rebuilds as upstream plus the ordered patches.
- **Patch**: A carry-patch entry: a branch with a position in the patch order and a status.
- **Rebuild**: A durable job that recreates the integration branch.
- **Durable job**: Background work that is recorded before its request returns, survives restarts and is retried with backoff. Rebuilds are the only durable jobs (§10).
- **Conflict report**: The structured description of why a rebase could not be done: files, kinds, and the landed changes involved.
- **Hub event**: A record of something the hub did (`parley.*` types), with a sequence number.
- **Handler**: The code registered for a job type that performs one attempt of a job.
- **Settlement**: The recording of an attempt's outcome: `completed`, `failed` or `dead_letter`.
- **Follow-up**: The one rebuild job a running rebuild may queue for the same workspace; it starts after the running job ends.
- **Waiting to retry**: The status `failed`; never an end state.

# Requirements

## Requirements

### REQ-1: Enqueue a durable job with dedup

**Rationale:** A caller asks for work once and must be able to trust that it is recorded, and that a workspace never accumulates pending jobs.

#### Criteria

1. [REQ-1.1] WHEN Enqueue is called inside a store transaction for a job type and a workspace that has no job of that type in queued, running or failed, THE job queue SHALL store a new job with status queued, retry_count 0, the given payload document, a null result document and created_at and updated_at equal to the clock's present, as part of that transaction, and return it
   → returns the job {id: a version 4 UUID, type, workspace_slug, status: 'queued', retry_count: 0, next_attempt_at: null, error: null, completed_at: null} and a nil error; the job is visible to other readers only after the caller's transaction commits
   Check: unit
   - setup: a queue of internal/jobs over a real store opened in t.TempDir(), a controlled clock, and no background dispatcher: the test runs single dispatcher passes
   ```
   in internal/jobs/enqueue_test.go: tx = store.begin(); j, err = q.Enqueue(tx, 'probe', 'w', payload); assert err == nil; assert j.status == 'queued' and j.retry_count == 0 and j.next_attempt_at == null and j.completed_at == null; assert j.id matches the UUID v4 pattern; assert q.Get(j.id) from outside the transaction is not found; tx.commit(); assert q.Get(j.id).payload == payload; a second case rolls the transaction back and asserts the job does not exist
   ```
1. [REQ-1.2] IF Enqueue is called for a job type and a workspace that already has a job of that type in queued, running or failed, THEN THE job queue SHALL store nothing and report a duplicate that names the existing job
   → returns a duplicate error from which the caller reads the existing job's id (errors.As to the queue's duplicate error type); the number of jobs of the workspace is unchanged
   Check: unit
   - setup: a queue of internal/jobs over a real store opened in t.TempDir(), a controlled clock, and no background dispatcher: the test runs single dispatcher passes
   - setup: a scripted handler registered for the job type 'probe' that records every call and returns what the case tells it
   ```
   in internal/jobs/enqueue_test.go, a table over the existing job's status {queued, running, failed}: _, err = q.Enqueue(tx, 'probe', 'w', p); assert err is the duplicate error and its job id == existing.id; assert count(jobs of 'w') == 1. Further rows where the enqueue succeeds: existing job completed, dead_letter or cancelled; existing pending job of workspace 'other'; existing pending job of 'w' with another job type
   ```
1. [REQ-1.3] IF several Enqueue calls for the same job type and workspace run at the same time in separate transactions, THEN THE job queue SHALL let exactly one of them store a job and report a duplicate to every other
   → exactly one call returns a job; each other call returns the duplicate error or, when its transaction lost a write conflict, is retried by the queue until it returns the duplicate error; one job of the workspace exists afterwards
   Check: integration
   - setup: a queue of internal/jobs over a real store file in t.TempDir()
   ```
   in internal/jobs/enqueue_test.go: start 16 goroutines that each begin a transaction, call q.Enqueue(tx, 'probe', 'w', p) and commit on success; assert exactly 1 success and 15 duplicate errors naming the winner's id; assert count(jobs of 'w') == 1
   ```
1. [REQ-1.4] WHEN a follow-up enqueue names a job of the same type and workspace that is running, and that job is the only job of the workspace in queued, running or failed, THE job queue SHALL store the follow-up as a new queued job
   → returns the new job with status 'queued' and an id different from the named job's
   Check: unit
   - setup: a queue of internal/jobs over a real store opened in t.TempDir(), a controlled clock, and no background dispatcher: the test runs single dispatcher passes
   - setup: a scripted handler registered for the job type 'probe' that records every call and returns what the case tells it
   ```
   in internal/jobs/enqueue_test.go: a = enqueue and claim a job of 'w' whose handler blocks; f, err = q.EnqueueFollowUp(tx, a.id, payload); assert err == nil; assert f.status == 'queued' and f.id != a.id and f.type == a.type and f.workspace_slug == 'w'
   ```
1. [REQ-1.5] IF a follow-up enqueue names a job that is not running, or names a running job while another job of the workspace is already queued or failed, THEN THE job queue SHALL store nothing and report a duplicate
   → returns the duplicate error naming a pending job of the workspace when one exists; returns a not-found error when the named job does not exist; the number of jobs is unchanged
   Check: unit
   - setup: a queue of internal/jobs over a real store opened in t.TempDir(), a controlled clock, and no background dispatcher: the test runs single dispatcher passes
   - setup: a scripted handler registered for the job type 'probe' that records every call and returns what the case tells it
   ```
   in internal/jobs/enqueue_test.go, a table: {named job queued, named job failed, named job completed with another job queued, named job running and a follow-up already queued} -> duplicate error; {unknown job id} -> not-found error; in every row count(jobs) is unchanged
   ```
1. [REQ-1.6] THE job queue SHALL for any job whose enqueueing transaction committed, return the same job, with the same id, payload and status, after the store is closed and opened again
   Check: integration
   - setup: a real store file in t.TempDir()
   ```
   in internal/jobs/store_test.go: enqueue three jobs for three workspaces and commit; close the store; open it again at the same path; build a new queue; for each: assert q.Get(id) equals the job returned at enqueue in id, type, workspace_slug, status, payload, created_at
   ```

### REQ-2: Run queued jobs on workers

**Rationale:** The hub executes its own jobs, a few at a time, and never two for one workspace.

#### Criteria

1. [REQ-2.1] WHEN a dispatcher pass finds a queued job whose type has a registered handler, while fewer than 4 jobs are running and no job of the same type and workspace is running, THE job queue SHALL claim the job by setting its status to running and emptying its result document, and call the handler once with the job and a context
   → the handler receives the job with status 'running' and its payload; a concurrent read of the job shows status 'running', result null and updated_at at the clock's present
   Check: unit
   - setup: a queue of internal/jobs over a real store opened in t.TempDir(), a controlled clock, and no background dispatcher: the test runs single dispatcher passes
   - setup: a scripted handler registered for the job type 'probe' that records every call and returns what the case tells it; the handler blocks until released
   ```
   in internal/jobs/queue_test.go: j = enqueue('probe','w', p); q.Pass(); wait until the handler is entered; assert handler.calls == [j.id] and the job it received has status 'running' and payload p; assert q.Get(j.id).status == 'running' and result == null
   ```
1. [REQ-2.2] WHEN a job is queued while the queue runs with its background dispatcher and a worker is free, THE job queue SHALL start the job's handler within 5 seconds
   → the handler is called no later than 5 seconds after the enqueueing transaction committed
   Check: integration
   - setup: a queue over a real store file in t.TempDir() with a handler for 'probe'
   ```
   in internal/jobs/queue_test.go: start q.Run(ctx) with the real clock and the default dispatcher interval; t0 = now; enqueue and commit; wait for the handler call with a 5 s deadline; assert it arrived; a second case enqueues without waking the dispatcher (the wake is disabled by a test option) and asserts the call still arrives within 5 s
   ```
1. [REQ-2.3] WHILE 4 jobs are running, THE job queue SHALL claim no further job, and claim the next queued job on the first dispatcher pass after one of the 4 has ended
   → at no moment are more than 4 handlers running; the fifth job stays 'queued' until a running job is settled
   Check: unit
   - setup: a queue of internal/jobs over a real store opened in t.TempDir(), a controlled clock, and no background dispatcher: the test runs single dispatcher passes
   - setup: a scripted handler registered for the job type 'probe' that records every call and returns what the case tells it; each handler blocks until released
   ```
   in internal/jobs/queue_test.go: enqueue jobs for workspaces w1..w6; q.Pass(); assert 4 handlers entered and jobs 5 and 6 are 'queued'; q.Pass() again; assert still 4; release handler 1; q.Pass(); assert job 5 is 'running' and job 6 'queued'; assert the maximum number of handlers observed running together == 4
   ```
1. [REQ-2.4] WHILE a job of a type and workspace is running, THE job queue SHALL leave every queued job of the same type and workspace unclaimed, and claim it on the first dispatcher pass after the running job has ended
   → the follow-up's handler call begins after the running job's settlement committed
   Check: unit
   - setup: a queue of internal/jobs over a real store opened in t.TempDir(), a controlled clock, and no background dispatcher: the test runs single dispatcher passes
   - setup: a scripted handler registered for the job type 'probe' that records every call and returns what the case tells it
   ```
   in internal/jobs/queue_test.go: a = enqueue('probe','w') and claim it (handler blocks); f = q.EnqueueFollowUp(tx, a.id, p); q.Pass(); assert f is 'queued' and handler.calls == [a.id]; release a; q.Pass(); assert q.Get(a.id).status == 'completed' and f is 'running'
   ```
1. [REQ-2.5] THE job queue SHALL for any queued job, let at most one worker claim it, however many dispatcher passes run at the same time
   → the handler is called exactly once per transition from queued to running
   Check: integration
   - setup: a queue over a real store file in t.TempDir()
   - setup: a scripted handler registered for the job type 'probe' that records every call and returns what the case tells it
   ```
   in internal/jobs/queue_test.go: enqueue one job; run 16 goroutines that each call q.Pass() at the same moment; release the handler; assert handler.calls has length 1; repeat for 50 jobs on 50 workspaces with the limit of 4 and assert every job id appears exactly once in handler.calls when all are completed
   ```
1. [REQ-2.6] THE job queue SHALL claim queued jobs in the order of created_at ascending, then id ascending
   Check: unit
   - setup: a queue of internal/jobs over a real store opened in t.TempDir(), a controlled clock, and no background dispatcher: the test runs single dispatcher passes
   - setup: a scripted handler registered for the job type 'probe' that records every call and returns what the case tells it
   ```
   in internal/jobs/queue_test.go: with the limit of 4 filled by blocking jobs, enqueue x at t, y at t+1s, z at t+1s for three further workspaces; release one running job at a time with a pass after each; assert the claim order is x, then the smaller id of {y, z}, then the other
   ```
1. [REQ-2.7] WHILE no handler is registered for a queued job's type, THE job queue SHALL leave the job queued and unchanged on every dispatcher pass, and claim it on the first pass after a handler for its type is registered
   → the job's status stays 'queued' and its updated_at does not change; the pass reports no error
   Check: unit

   in internal/jobs/queue_test.go: j = enqueue('nohandler','w'); q.Pass(); q.Pass(); assert q.Get(j.id) equals j; q.Register('nohandler', h); q.Pass(); assert h.calls == [j.id]

   ```

### REQ-3: Settle the outcome of an attempt

**Rationale:** A failure that may pass is retried with growing delays; one that cannot pass ends the job at once, where a person can look at it and requeue it.

#### Criteria

1. [REQ-3.1] WHEN the handler of a running job returns nil, THE job queue SHALL set the job's status to completed, clear error and the failure detail, set completed_at to the clock's present, leave next_attempt_at null and keep the result document the handler stored
   → a read of the job returns status 'completed', error null, detail null, completed_at set, retry_count unchanged
   Check: unit
   - setup: a queue of internal/jobs over a real store opened in t.TempDir(), a controlled clock, and no background dispatcher: the test runs single dispatcher passes
   - setup: a scripted handler registered for the job type 'probe' that records every call and returns what the case tells it
   ```
   in internal/jobs/settle_test.go: a job that failed once retryably (retry_count 1, error set) runs again and its handler stores result R and returns nil; assert status == 'completed'; error == null; detail == null; completed_at == clock.now; retry_count == 1; result == R
   ```
1. [REQ-3.2] WHEN the handler of a running job returns an error that is not marked permanent, and the job's retry_count is below 20, THE job queue SHALL set the job's status to failed, raise retry_count by one to n, set next_attempt_at to the clock's present plus min(2 seconds × 2 to the power n, 2 hours), store the error's text in error, replace the failure detail by the one the error carries or clear it, and leave completed_at null
   → after the n-th retryable failure next_attempt_at − now is 4 s for n=1, 8 s for n=2, 16 s for n=3, 4096 s for n=11, 7200 s for n=12 and 7200 s for n=20
   Check: unit
   - setup: a queue of internal/jobs over a real store opened in t.TempDir(), a controlled clock, and no background dispatcher: the test runs single dispatcher passes
   - setup: a scripted handler registered for the job type 'probe' that records every call and returns what the case tells it
   ```
   in internal/jobs/settle_test.go, a table over retry_count before the attempt {0, 1, 2, 10, 11, 19}: settle a retryable error 'boom'; assert status == 'failed'; retry_count == before+1; next_attempt_at − clock.now == {4s, 8s, 16s, 4096s, 7200s, 7200s}; error == 'boom'; completed_at == null. One more row: an error carrying detail D after a failure that stored detail C -> detail == D; then an error with no detail -> detail == null
   ```
1. [REQ-3.3] IF the handler of a running job returns an error that is not marked permanent, and the job's retry_count is 20, THEN THE job queue SHALL set the job's status to dead_letter with retry_count still 20, store the error's text, set completed_at and leave next_attempt_at null
   → a read returns status 'dead_letter', retry_count 20, next_attempt_at null, completed_at set; no later dispatcher pass calls the handler for this job
   Check: unit
   - setup: a queue of internal/jobs over a real store opened in t.TempDir(), a controlled clock, and no background dispatcher: the test runs single dispatcher passes
   - setup: a scripted handler registered for the job type 'probe' that records every call and returns what the case tells it
   ```
   in internal/jobs/settle_test.go: drive one job through 20 retryable failures, advancing the clock to each next_attempt_at; assert it is 'failed' with retry_count 20; advance and fail a 21st time; assert status == 'dead_letter' and retry_count == 20 and completed_at != null and next_attempt_at == null; advance the clock by 3 h and run a pass; assert handler.calls has length 21
   ```
1. [REQ-3.4] IF the handler of a running job returns an error marked permanent, THEN THE job queue SHALL set the job's status to dead_letter without changing retry_count, store the error's text and the detail document the error carries, set completed_at and never retry the job
   → a read returns status 'dead_letter', retry_count as before the attempt, error the text, detail the document, completed_at set, next_attempt_at null
   Check: unit
   - setup: a queue of internal/jobs over a real store opened in t.TempDir(), a controlled clock, and no background dispatcher: the test runs single dispatcher passes
   - setup: a scripted handler registered for the job type 'probe' that records every call and returns what the case tells it
   ```
   in internal/jobs/settle_test.go, a table over retry_count before {0, 3}: the handler returns jobs.Permanent(err 'conflict') carrying detail D; assert status == 'dead_letter'; retry_count == before; error == 'conflict'; detail == D; completed_at == clock.now; advance 3 h; q.Pass(); assert the handler was not called again
   ```
1. [REQ-3.5] IF the handler of a running job panics, THEN THE job queue SHALL recover the panic, settle the attempt as a retryable failure whose error text contains the panic value, and keep serving other jobs
   → the job is 'failed' (or 'dead_letter' when retry_count was 20) with error containing the panic value; the process does not exit; a job of another workspace queued afterwards completes
   Check: unit
   - setup: a queue of internal/jobs over a real store opened in t.TempDir(), a controlled clock, and no background dispatcher: the test runs single dispatcher passes
   - setup: a scripted handler registered for the job type 'probe' that records every call and returns what the case tells it

   in internal/jobs/settle_test.go: the handler panics with 'kaboom' for workspace 'w'; q.Pass(); assert q.Get(j.id).status == 'failed' and error contains 'kaboom' and retry_count == 1; enqueue a job for 'w2' with a handler result of nil; q.Pass(); assert it is 'completed'

1. [REQ-3.6] WHEN an attempt is settled and the job's type registered a settlement hook, THE job queue SHALL call the hook once inside the store transaction of the settlement, with the job as the settlement leaves it and a flag that is true only when the new status is failed

   - setup: a queue of internal/jobs over a real store opened in t.TempDir(), a controlled clock, and no background dispatcher: the test runs single dispatcher passes

   - setup: a scripted handler registered for the job type 'probe' that records every call and returns what the case tells it
   ```
   in internal/jobs/settle_test.go: inside the handler: q.SetResult(ctx, j.id, R1); the test reads q.Get(j.id).result == R1 while the handler blocks; q.SetResult(ctx, j.id, R2); read == R2; release; after completion result == R2; then q.SetResult(ctx, j.id, R3) returns the not-running error and result is still R2; a later claim of a requeued job shows result null

### REQ-4: Recover after a crash and stop at shutdown

**Rationale:** A job must not be lost or stuck because the hub stopped while it ran.

#### Criteria

1. [REQ-4.1] WHEN the queue's start hook runs and the store holds jobs with status running, THE job queue SHALL set each of them to queued with retry_count, error, payload and created_at unchanged, before the dispatcher makes its first pass, and leave jobs in every other status untouched
   → the hook returns nil; afterwards no job is 'running'; a job that was 'failed' keeps its next_attempt_at
   Check: integration
   - setup: a real store file in t.TempDir()
   - setup: a scripted handler registered for the job type 'probe' that records every call and returns what the case tells it; handlers of the first queue block for ever
   ```
   in internal/jobs/lifecycle_test.go: with a first queue, bring jobs into {running with retry_count 0, running with retry_count 3 and an error text, failed, queued, completed, dead_letter, cancelled}; abandon that queue without settling; close and reopen the store; q2 = new queue; assert q2.Recover(ctx) == nil; assert both running jobs are 'queued' with retry_count {0, 3} and the error text kept; assert the five others are unchanged field by field
   ```
1. [REQ-4.2] WHEN the dispatcher runs after a recovery that returned a job to queued, THE job queue SHALL claim the job and call its handler again from the start with the same job id and payload and an empty result document
   → the handler is called once by the new queue for that job; when it returns nil the job is 'completed' with the retry_count it had before the stop
   Check: integration
   - setup: a real store file in t.TempDir()
   - setup: a scripted handler registered for the job type 'probe' that records every call and returns what the case tells it
   ```
   in internal/jobs/lifecycle_test.go: queue 1 claims job j (payload P), its handler stores result R and then blocks for ever; abandon queue 1, close and reopen the store; q2 = new queue with a handler that returns nil; q2.Recover(ctx); q2.Pass(); assert handler2.calls == [j.id] and the job it received has payload P and result null and retry_count 0; assert q2.Get(j.id).status == 'completed' and retry_count == 0
   ```
1. [REQ-4.3] WHEN the hub's shutdown reaches the queue while handlers are running, THE job queue SHALL claim no further job, wait up to 30 seconds for the running handlers, settle the outcome of each handler that returns in that time, and stop when all have returned
   → the queue's run function returns as soon as the last running handler has returned and was settled; a job queued before or during the shutdown stays 'queued'
   Check: unit
   - setup: a queue of internal/jobs over a real store opened in t.TempDir(), a controlled clock, and no background dispatcher: the test runs single dispatcher passes
   - setup: a scripted handler registered for the job type 'probe' that records every call and returns what the case tells it
   ```
   in internal/jobs/lifecycle_test.go: start q.Run(ctx) with a controlled clock; job a is running (handler blocks), job b is queued for another workspace behind a full limit or enqueued after the cancel; cancel ctx; assert Run has not returned; q.Pass() has no effect: b stays 'queued'; release a's handler with nil; assert Run returns; assert a is 'completed' and b is 'queued' and b's handler was never called
   ```
1. [REQ-4.4] IF a handler is still running 30 seconds after the shutdown reached the queue, THEN THE job queue SHALL cancel that handler's context, stop without settling the attempt, and leave the job with status running in the store
   → the run function returns at 30 seconds; the job's status, retry_count and error are as they were while it ran; an outcome the handler returns afterwards is dropped
   Check: unit
   - setup: a queue of internal/jobs over a real store opened in t.TempDir(), a controlled clock, and no background dispatcher: the test runs single dispatcher passes
   - setup: a scripted handler registered for the job type 'probe' that records every call and returns what the case tells it
   ```
   in internal/jobs/lifecycle_test.go: job a is running with a handler that waits for its context; cancel the run context; advance the clock 29 s; assert Run has not returned and the handler's context is not done; advance to 30 s; assert the handler's context is done and Run returns; let the handler return an error; assert q.Get(a.id).status == 'running' and retry_count == 0 and error == null
   ```

### REQ-5: Count jobs and remove them with their workspace

**Rationale:** Operators watch the depth of the queue, and a deleted workspace must leave no job behind.

#### Criteria

1. [REQ-5.1] WHEN a caller asks the queue for its depth, THE job queue SHALL return, for every registered job type, the number of jobs in each of the statuses queued, running, failed, completed, dead_letter and cancelled, with 0 for a status that has none
   → a map from job type to the six statuses, each with a count; all six keys are present for every registered type, also when the type has no job
   Check: unit
   - setup: a queue of internal/jobs over a real store opened in t.TempDir(), a controlled clock, and no background dispatcher: the test runs single dispatcher passes

## Execution Paths

### PATH-1: A developer submits a rebuild and waits through a retry

1. **developer** runs parley rebuild submit <slug> --wait on a carry-patch workspace with one active patch
2. **parley CLI** sends POST /api/v1/workspaces/<slug>/rebuild
3. **parleyd** stores the job as queued together with parley.rebuild.enqueue and answers 202 with the job record
4. **parleyd** claims the job on a worker and runs the handler, which fails with a retryable error; the job becomes failed with retry_count 1 and next_attempt_at 4 seconds later
5. **parley CLI** polls GET /api/v1/workspaces/<slug>/rebuilds/<id>, sees failed and keeps polling
6. **parleyd** returns the job to queued when next_attempt_at is reached, runs the handler again and settles the job as completed
7. **parley CLI** prints the final job record with status completed and exits 0

**Smoke check — real components (must not be mocked):** parley CLI (cli.Run), HTTP router with authentication, access and the rebuild routes, shared rebuild enqueue, job queue with its background dispatcher, transactional store, event log

**Setup:**

- a hub started in-process on 127.0.0.1:0 with a controlled clock and a real store in t.TempDir()
- a ready carry-patch workspace with one active patch, created through the hub
- the handler registered for the job type 'rebuild' is a scripted test handler that returns a retryable error on its first call and nil on its second (the rebuild handler of package 34 replaces it in production)

**End state:**

- the command's exit status is 0 and stdout is one job record with status 'completed' and retry_count 1
- the handler was called twice with the same job id
- the event log holds one parley.rebuild.enqueue for the job
- GET /api/v1/workspaces/<slug>/rebuilds lists the job once

**Pseudocode:**

```
in test/e2e/rebuild_jobs_test.go: start the hub; create the workspace and patch; run cli.Run(['rebuild','submit',slug,'--wait','--poll-interval','20ms']) in a goroutine; wait until GET the job shows 'failed' with retry_count 1 and next_attempt_at == failure time + 4s; advance the clock by 4s; wait for the command; assert code == 0; assert json(stdout).status == 'completed' and retry_count == 1; assert handler.calls == 2; assert the events of type parley.rebuild.enqueue for the job == 1
```

### PATH-2: A rebuild job survives a restart of the hub

1. **agent** sends POST /workspaces/:slug/rebuild and receives 202 with the job record
2. **parleyd** claims the job; the handler is running when the hub stops
3. **operator** starts the hub again on the same data directory
4. **parleyd** returns the job from running to queued with retry_count unchanged before any worker starts, then claims it and runs the handler from the start
5. **agent** reads GET /workspaces/:slug/rebuilds/:id and sees status completed

**Smoke check — real components (must not be mocked):** HTTP router with the rebuild routes, job queue with crash recovery as a start hook, transactional store on disk, hub start and shutdown of internal/hub

**Setup:**

- a hub started in-process on a data directory in t.TempDir()
- a ready carry-patch workspace with one active patch
- a scripted handler for 'rebuild' that never returns and ignores its context in the first hub, and returns nil in the second

**End state:**

- after the restart the job has status 'completed', retry_count 0 and the id the POST returned
- the second hub's handler was called once, with the payload captured at enqueue
- no job has status 'running'

**Pseudocode:**

```
in test/e2e/rebuild_jobs_test.go: start hub 1; id = POST rebuild; wait until GET shows 'running'; stop hub 1 with its shutdown grace cut short by the controlled clock; open the store directly and assert the job is still 'running'; start hub 2 on the same directory; wait until GET id shows 'completed'; assert retry_count == 0; assert handler2.calls == [id]
```

### PATH-3: An agent cancels a queued rebuild and requeues a dead-lettered one

1. **agent** sends POST /workspaces/:slug/rebuild; the handler fails with a permanent error
2. **parleyd** settles the job as dead_letter with the error text and the failure detail
3. **agent** sends POST /workspaces/:slug/rebuild again and receives 202 with a second job, then POST requeue of the first job
4. **parleyd** answers the requeue with 409 concurrent_rebuild because the second job is queued
5. **agent** sends DELETE /workspaces/:slug/rebuilds/<second id> twice
6. **parleyd** answers 200 with status cancelled and parley.rebuild.cancel, then 409 job_not_cancellable
7. **agent** sends POST requeue of the first job again
8. **parleyd** answers 200 with status queued, retry_count 0, error and conflict null, and writes parley.rebuild.requeue

**Smoke check — real components (must not be mocked):** HTTP router with authentication, access and the rebuild routes, shared rebuild enqueue, job queue, transactional store, event log

**Setup:**

- a hub started in-process with a real store in t.TempDir()
- a ready carry-patch workspace with one active patch
- a scripted handler for 'rebuild' that returns a permanent error with a detail document on its first call and blocks on later calls; the dispatcher is paused by the test while the second job must stay queued

**End state:**

- the first job is 'queued' with retry_count 0 (the dispatcher is still paused), error null and conflict null
- the second job is 'cancelled' with completed_at set
- the event log holds two parley.rebuild.enqueue, one parley.rebuild.cancel and one parley.rebuild.requeue for the workspace
- GET /workspaces/:slug/rebuilds returns the two jobs, the second first

**Pseudocode:**

```
in test/e2e/rebuild_jobs_test.go: a = POST rebuild; wait until GET a shows 'dead_letter' with conflict != null; pause the dispatcher; b = POST rebuild; assert 202; assert POST a/requeue is 409 'concurrent_rebuild'; assert DELETE b is 200 'cancelled'; assert DELETE b is 409 'job_not_cancellable'; r = POST a/requeue; assert 200 and status 'queued' and retry_count 0 and error == null and conflict == null; assert the counts of the three event types; assert the list order is [b, a]
```


# Tasks

## Test Commands

- **all_tests:** `go test ./... -count=1`
- **linter:** `golangci-lint run ./...`
- **spec_tests:** `go test ./internal/jobs/... ./internal/carrypatch/... ./internal/cli/... ./test/e2e/... -count=1`

## Dependencies

- `31` — carry-patch workspaces, the patch list, the integration branch accessor, the RebuildEnqueuer interface this package implements and the common carry-patch precondition check the rebuild routes call
- `09` — the parley rebuild commands are built on its command helper, HTTP client, output, exit codes and shared --wait
- `52` — parley.rebuild.enqueue, cancel and requeue are written through its event component in the transaction of the state change
- `14` — registers the remover of a workspace's job records with the removers of owned data it declares in internal/workspace

### 1. Store durable jobs and enqueue them with dedup (implement)

**Criteria:** REQ-1

**Steps:**

- 1.1 Add the enqueue behaviours to internal/jobs/enqueue_test.go and the reopen behaviour to internal/jobs/store_test.go, against a real store in t.TempDir(), and confirm they fail
- 1.2 Define the job in internal/jobs/job.go: id, type, workspace slug, status (queued, running, failed, completed, dead_letter, cancelled), payload, result and failure-detail documents held as opaque JSON, retry_count, next_attempt_at, error, created_at, updated_at, completed_at; say which statuses are pending (queued, running, failed) and which are final
- 1.3 Register the schema migration for the job table with internal/store, with an index that serves 'pending jobs of a type and workspace' and 'jobs of a workspace newest first'
- 1.4 Build the queue value in internal/jobs/queue.go from the store, a replaceable clock and a logger; expose Get by id and a read of one workspace's jobs of a type with an optional status filter, ordered by created_at descending then id descending, with the paging inputs the list helper of internal/server needs
- 1.5 Implement Enqueue(tx, type, workspace, payload): inside the caller's transaction, refuse with a duplicate error carrying the existing job's id when a pending job of that type and workspace exists, else insert a queued job with a random version 4 UUID made with crypto/rand, retry_count 0 and both timestamps at the clock's present
- 1.6 Make dedup hold under concurrency: the check and the insert are one atomic step in the store, so that of several concurrent enqueues one stores a job and every other reports the duplicate
- 1.7 Implement EnqueueFollowUp(tx, runningJobID, payload): allowed only when the named job is running and is the workspace's only pending job; a not-found error for an unknown id; the duplicate error otherwise
- 1.8 Return errors from every operation; nothing in internal/jobs ends the process

### 2. Claim queued jobs and run them on workers (implement)

**Criteria:** REQ-2

**Steps:**

- 2.1 Add the claiming behaviours to internal/jobs/queue_test.go with a scripted handler and single dispatcher passes under a controlled clock, and confirm they fail
- 2.2 Define the handler interface in internal/jobs/handler.go: one operation that runs an attempt (context and job in, error out) and one settlement hook (transaction, job, will-retry flag in, error out); Register(type, handler) on the queue
- 2.3 Implement one dispatcher pass (Pass): first return every failed job whose next_attempt_at is at or before the clock's present to queued with next_attempt_at null; then claim queued jobs in the order created_at ascending, id ascending
- 2.4 A claim is one conditional update from queued to running that also empties the result document and sets updated_at; a pass whose update changed no row lost the claim and moves on
- 2.5 Skip a queued job while 4 jobs are running, while another job of its type and workspace is running, and while its type has no registered handler; such a job is left unchanged
- 2.6 Run each claimed job's handler on its own goroutine with a context the queue can cancel; count running handlers so that the limit of 4 holds across concurrent passes
- 2.7 Implement Run(ctx): a background dispatcher that makes a pass at least once per second and whenever it is woken; wake it after an enqueue's transaction commits, after a requeue and after every settlement; give tests an option to set the interval and to disable the wake
- 2.8 Settle a handler that returns nil as completed (status and completed_at in one transaction) so that the limit of 4 and the one-per-workspace rule can be observed end to end; the settlement of failures, the hook and the backoff are the next task's

**Touches:**

- `internal/jobs/queue.go`
- `internal/jobs/queue_test.go`

### 3. Settle attempts: complete, retry with backoff, dead-letter (implement)

**Criteria:** REQ-3

**Steps:**

- 3.1 Add the settlement behaviours to internal/jobs/settle_test.go, the backoff table among them, and confirm they fail
- 3.2 Add the error markers in internal/jobs/errors.go: Permanent(err) marks an error permanent, WithDetail(err, document) attaches a detail document; any other error is retryable
- 3.3 Settle a nil return as completed: clear error and detail, set completed_at, keep retry_count and the stored result
- 3.4 Settle a retryable error with retry_count below 20 as failed: raise retry_count to n, set next_attempt_at to the present plus min(2 s × 2ⁿ, 2 h), store the error text, replace or clear the detail
- 3.5 Settle a retryable error at retry_count 20, and every permanent error, as dead_letter: retry_count unchanged, error text and detail stored, completed_at set, next_attempt_at null
- 3.6 Recover a panic of a handler and settle it as a retryable error whose text contains the panic value
- 3.7 Do each settlement in one store transaction and call the type's settlement hook inside it with the job as settled and will_retry true only for failed; run the hook under a savepoint so that a hook that returns an error or panics has its writes undone, is logged with the job id, and the settlement still commits
- 3.8 Implement SetResult(ctx, jobID, document): replaces the result document of a running job and returns a not-running error for a job in any other status
- 3.9 Wake the dispatcher after every settlement so that a follow-up or a waiting job starts on the next pass

### 6. Queue rebuilds through one shared enqueue and POST /workspaces/:slug/rebuild (implement)

**Criteria:** REQ-6

**Steps:**

- 6.1 Add the submit behaviours to internal/carrypatch/rebuild_routes_test.go and the shared-enqueue and event behaviours to internal/carrypatch/rebuild_enqueue_test.go, against a real router, store and event component, and confirm they fail
- 6.2 Define the job type name 'rebuild' and the rebuild payload (strategy, fail_mode, integration_branch, submitted_by, and the session id given at enqueue, which the job record does not show and package 34 puts on the job's events) in internal/carrypatch/rebuild_enqueue.go
- 6.3 Implement EnqueueRebuild(ctx, slug, options) as the implementation of the interface RebuildEnqueuer that package 31 declares in internal/carrypatch/rebuild_enqueuer.go, with that file's options and result types: options carry an optional strategy and fail mode, submitted_by, the event's actor and session, and an optional follow-up-of job id; an empty strategy or fail mode falls back to the workspace settings rebuild_strategy (default rebase) and rebuild_fail_mode (default fail_fast); the integration branch is what IntegrationBranch of package 31 returns for the workspace
- 6.4 In one store transaction: enqueue through internal/jobs (Enqueue, or EnqueueFollowUp when a follow-up-of id is given) and write parley.rebuild.enqueue through the event component of package 52 with resource_type rebuild, the job id, the given actor and session, and metadata submitted_by, strategy, fail_mode and patch_count (patches in active or conflict)
- 6.5 On the queue's duplicate error return a result that says nothing was queued and names the existing job's id, with a nil error and no event; do not apply the no_active_patches check here
- 6.6 Build the rebuild job record in internal/carrypatch/rebuild_record.go from a job: the payload's four fields, status, retry_count, next_attempt_at, error (null when empty), conflict (the failure detail), the three timestamps as RFC 3339 UTC whole seconds, and the result document's members under their record names with the defaults null, 0, false and [] for absent ones; every field is always present

- 6.9 Mount the route on the hub's router where the other carry-patch routes are mounted, and register the implementation as the hub's RebuildEnqueuer through the registration call of package 31, replacing its default, so that packages 32, 34, 36 and 37 queue through it

### 8. Cancel queued jobs and requeue dead-lettered ones (implement)

**Criteria:** REQ-8

**Steps:**

- 8.1 Add the cancel and requeue behaviours, the cancel-against-claim race among them, to internal/carrypatch/rebuild_routes_test.go and confirm they fail
- 8.2 Implement Cancel(tx, jobID) in internal/jobs/cancel.go as one conditional update from queued to cancelled that sets completed_at; when no row changed, return a not-cancellable error; the same condition is what a claim uses, so exactly one of the two takes effect
- 8.3 Implement Requeue(tx, jobID): a job that is not dead_letter returns a not-requeueable error; then, when another pending job of the type and workspace exists, the duplicate error; otherwise set queued, retry_count 0, error, detail, next_attempt_at and completed_at null, keeping id, created_at and payload; wake the dispatcher after the commit
- 8.4 Add DELETE /workspaces/:slug/rebuilds/:id: scope rebuilds:write, write access, the carry-patch precondition check for a write route, the job lookup, then Cancel and parley.rebuild.cancel (actor the caller, no metadata) in one transaction; 200 with the record, or 409 job_not_cancellable
- 8.5 Add POST /workspaces/:slug/rebuilds/:id/requeue (no body) with the same checks, then Requeue and parley.rebuild.requeue (actor the caller, no metadata) in one transaction; 200 with the record, 409 job_not_requeueable, or 409 concurrent_rebuild
